learningObjective: Explain the mechanism of speculative decoding and its correctness property.
stem: Which description of speculative decoding for LLM inference is correct?

options.text: A small 'draft' model is used to generate k candidate tokens at once by predicting all k positions in parallel; the target model is then used only to compute a probability for the whole k-token sequence, and the whole sequence is accepted if the joint probability exceeds a threshold.

Speculative decoding uses a distilled quantized version of the target model as the sole decoder; the 'speculative' name refers to running INT4 arithmetic that may be numerically wrong but recovers quality through calibration.

A smaller/faster draft model proposes k tokens autoregressively. The target model runs one forward pass on all k proposed positions (like a k-token prefill) and, using its own logits, accepts a prefix of the proposal by comparing probabilities per position via rejection sampling; the accepted prefix has the exact same distribution as target-only sampling.

The target model itself decodes in parallel over k positions by conditioning each of the k output positions on the same input hidden state; the 'draft' terminology refers to these draft positions being generated in one shot before being ranked.

explanation: Speculative decoding (Leviathan et al., 2023) uses a small/fast draft model to propose k tokens autoregressively, then does a single target-model forward on all k positions (equivalent to k-token prefill for the target). Using rejection sampling comparing draft and target probabilities per position, a prefix of the proposal is accepted; the retained distribution is exactly the target model's sampling distribution. On acceptance of j <= k tokens, one target forward yields j+1 output tokens (j accepted plus one new sampled by target when rejection happens), improving throughput without changing sampling semantics.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: draft model is used autoregressively for k steps; acceptance is per-token via rejection sampling.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: describes model quantization, not speculative decoding.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: describes non-autoregressive generation, not spec decoding.

assumptions: Both draft and target use the same vocabulary and tokenization.
nonImplications: Does not imply arbitrary speedup; benefit depends on the acceptance rate.
Does not imply the draft model's outputs are ever visible; only accepted tokens flow to the user.
